newsitem.title: UK: Singapore refinery margins revive sharply - IEA.
newsitem.headline: Singapore refinery margins revive sharply - IEA.

text.p: Refinery profit margins jumped in Singapore in February, increasing by more than $4 a barrel from January's low to February's high, on falling crude prices and fairly stable product prices, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Friday.
Average margins rose modestly in the U.S. Gulf but declined in the Mediterranean and northwest Europe, the IEA said in a Monthly Oil Market Report.
It said the exceptionally strong recovery in Asia was the result of of major product prices remaining little changed or declining only slightly while crude prices fell appreciably.
Average margins in Singapore for Dubai hydroskimming rose to $0.78 a barrel, an increase of $1.47 a barrel, while those for Dubai cracking rose to $3.43 a barrel, an increase of $1.72,
In Rotterdam and the Mediterranean, average refining margins decreased as a result of the steep decline in distillate prices, which fell by considerably more than crude, the report said.
However the fall in distillates was partly offset by relative strength in gasoline and naphtha markets, which fell by less than those of crude.

In the Mediterranean, margins recovered in the second half of the month, mainly due to weakening sour crudes and strengthening gasoline, following their steep decline in late January and early February.

The differential between the cracking margin and the hydroskimming margin widened for the third successive month, to $1.39 a barrel and $1.41 a barrel, for Rotterdam and the Mediterranean respectively, reflecting weakness in European fuel oil markets.
Margins in northwest Europe for Brent hydroskimming slipped to $0.68 and for Brent cracking fell to $0.71. decreases of $0.45 and $0.38 respectively.
Margins in the U.S. Gulf for Brent cracking rose to $0.36 a barrel and for WTI cracking to $0.76 a barrel, increases of $0.09 and $0.44 respectively.
Margins in the Med for Urals hydroskimming fell to $0.40 and for Urals cracking to $1.00, declines of $0.35 and $0.22 respectively.
